question: Evaluate $\int \frac{dx}{1 + \sin x + \cos x}$.
explanation:
Use the substitution $t=\tan\frac{x}{2}$.

Then $\sin x=\frac{2t}{1+t^2}$, $\cos x=\frac{1-t^2}{1+t^2}$ and $dx=\frac{2}{1+t^2}dt$.

Substitute into the integral to obtain $\int \frac{2}{2+2t}dt$.

This simplifies to $\int \frac{1}{1+t}dt$.

$=\ln|1+t|+C$.

Substitute back $t=\tan\frac{x}{2}$ to get $\ln\left|1+\tan\frac{x}{2}\right|+C$.
